support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head ridge land
support_bodies.rationale: The 1.00 mm apex land of the -X rail's slide-head ridge - the Z seam's one down-looking face on this piece. Lifting a seated back-top lands the ridge in the groove in that piece's foot on both 45 degree flanks at once (`hook_apex_flat`), so the land carries the joint's bearing against lift along the rail's whole run. Its two interface islands are the one run either side of the PRV passage, the 12 mm opening that has to cross this flank, and that same opening is what lets the body root on the bed outside the flank instead of on the arm's own under-flare.

support_bodies.name: east Z-seam slide-head ridge land
support_bodies.rationale: The +X rail's ridge land, the mirror of the west one and continuous over its whole run because nothing crosses this flank. With no opening through the wall beside it the body has no lane to the bed, so it roots on the arm's own 45 degree under-flare 6.00 mm below the land it carries. The contact is the land's own 1.2 mm across where the square catch's was 4.4.

support_bodies.name: west lower Y-seam socket collar crown
support_bodies.rationale: The complete crown of the lower west Y-seam socket collar. It keeps the collar's full structural stock over the cross-pin's square slide slot and its blind heat-set pocket, so the pin registers on a square pass envelope and the M3 bears on a whole section; pitching the crown into a roof would erase that envelope. Its one tree grows from the bed through the open cavity.

support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The flat underside of the -X rail's slide head - the Z seam's one down-looking face, and the whole of the screwless bottom-to-top joint's bearing against lift. Lifting a seated front-top lands its foot's flat top face on this one along the rail's entire run, and pitching the catch would turn it into a cam. The arm under it already returns to the wall on a 45 degree under-flare, so there is no wall-rooted wedge left to grow, and nothing crosses this flank at the catch's height to give the body a lane to the bed: it roots on that under-flare 8.00 mm below the catch. It, its east mirror and back-bottom's east catch are the three material-rooted supports in the box and the only bodies outside the 15 mm band, and they are what the campaign owes its next fix.

support_bodies.name: collet-plate stop and pump-bay lintel tree
support_bodies.rationale: The lower contact carries the exact 1 mm flat land that stops the steel collet plate and defines its Z datum; its fore edge is already raked at 45 degrees. The upper contact is the lintel that closes the full-width removable pump-cartridge bay while carrying the display above it. A support-free gable across that deep opening would occupy the rectangular cartridge-withdrawal or display envelope. The two contacts share one long bed-rooted tree, so neither hides a separate short or material-rooted support.

support_bodies.name: west Y-seam ceiling-tongue socket crown
support_bodies.rationale: This flat is the complete crown of the upper west Y-seam socket collar, and the ceiling tongue rises directly from it. The crown preserves the socket's full registration web and gives the tongue its load-bearing root; its one removable tree grows from the bed through the open enclosure.

support_bodies.name: X- pump boss-bearing shoulder
support_bodies.rationale: The flat annular shoulder bears axially on the fitted pump boss while the complete octagonal wall locates X, Y and yaw. Chamfering the shoulder would trade away bearing area rather than remove an accidental overhang; its centre bore remains open for direct support removal.
